Alex / Kimberly —

Per Alex's ask, below is a concise inline benchmark (representative, nominal $/1M token equivalents for generative workloads). We'll attach the full spreadsheet with model equivalencies and assumptions. All numbers are approximate list rates or observed managed-host run-rates as of Oct 2027; final contract pricing can vary with commit and model selection.

Host / Representative model class -> $ per 1M tokens (generation-weighted)
- OpenAI (capability-tier mix, equivalent GPT-4.1-like): $900–1,300 / 1M
- Anthropic (Claude-3-class): $700–1,000 / 1M
- Major managed open-model hosts (HF-managed, Vertex-like inference): $350–600 / 1M
- Self-hosted + infra ops (unmanaged): $120–300 / 1M (high ops + infra variability)
- Redwood Hosted (production profile, throughput optimizations, prefix caching): list $220 / 1M; committed tier $160 / 1M

Suggested pilot offer (30-day, capped):
- Pilot scope: up to 30M tokens (generation + embeddings mix as discussed)
- Pilot price: $120 / 1M tokens for the pilot (one-time introductory rate)
- Overage: $150 / 1M after 30M cap during pilot
- Post-pilot: proposed committed pricing band $140–$160 / 1M at 12-mo commit for 40M+/mo

Rationale / notes:
- The OpenAI/Anthropic rate lines reflect hosted high-capacity models (higher latency/quality tiers).
- Managed open-model hosts provide better unit economics than OpenAI for many workloads but often require model selection and quantization tradeoffs.
- Redwood's value proposition at the committed tier is predictable run-rates, autoscaling for spikes, and integrated cost/latency observability (helps reduce hidden ops costs).

Attachments: redwood-hosting-pricing-vs-hosts-20271019.xlsx (detailed sheet with assumptions)
